invariant: Every SVEK result, including the all-autonomous top-level state graph, is normalized from its complete painted minimum. The primitive occupying that minimum determines the translation: an ordinary rectangle contributes x-1, while an initial-state ellipse contributes its image x without rectangle overscan. Rank direction may change which primitive is leftmost, but it never changes whether SvekResult applies moveDelta. The five-pixel Cuca positive-axis compatibility margin remains a file-level addition for live-cluster composition and is independent of painted-origin normalization.
causal_divergence: Rust normalizes autonomous inner regions and mixed live-cluster roots, but skips normalize_autonomous_scope for an all-autonomous outer root. Its legacy initial origin is x=7. In top-to-bottom fixtures a leftmost composite rectangle contributes x-1, accidentally yielding Java's visible x=6 and hiding the omission. In left-to-right fixtures the root initial-state ellipse is leftmost and has no negative overscan, so every emitted primitive is one pixel too far right. The legacy width calculation also retains one extra pixel on each horizontal side and one vertical side, producing the repeated +2 width and +1 height checker failures. Alignment, raw-link metadata, and label text are incidental to this shared root-envelope divergence.

Add a regression covering an all-autonomous left-to-right root whose initial ellipse is the minimum, while retaining a top-to-bottom rectangle-minimum control. Verify the preserved rank/alignment checker matrix and complete renderer tests.
